utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. The witness could be brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It doesn't seem to be working.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. Would you please read aloud the affirmation on the card that is now given to you. I'm sorry, Mr. Djurdjic, you have a -- if you could just hold that a moment. Just hold. Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour. I didn't have the interpretation in the headphones. I didn't hear that you had called the witness to come in. I just wanted to raise an issue left over from last Wednesday in connection with the witnesses coming to testify under subpoena; namely, the decision of the Chamber regarding such -- the issuance of a subpoena has not reached us. Out of the nine witnesses, for five a subpoena was suggested, and today we have a proposal for another witness, an additional witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I ask you, Mr. Djurdjic, that we hold this and finish the swearing-in of the present witness and allow him to sit down. Thank you. Sir, would you please read aloud the affirmation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please sit. Now, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. As we are talking about confidential material, I would propose a closed session, even though -- I'm in your hands, Your Honour, to decide about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Closed.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I believe we're now in open session. I believe Mr. Stamp has some questions for you. Yes, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours. With your leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Golubovic.

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I would like you to state your name and your date of birth for the record, if you will, please.

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: My name is Caslav Golubovic. I was born on the 15th of May, 1937.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And in 1998 and 1999 you were the chief of the secretariat of the interior for the area of Bor, the municipality of Bor, in Serbia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: I was chief of the SUP in Bor, but it covered the territory of the whole district, not just the municipality of Bor.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I see. And presently you are retired, I take it?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, do you recall giving a statement to investigators of the Office of the Prosecution of this Tribunal on the 7th and 14th of August, 2002?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: I do recall that. I was in the Tribunal offices.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And that statement was read over to you in the Serbian language, and you accepted it as your statement by signing it; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And since you have returned here, you have been here in The Hague over the last few days, have you had an opportunity to review this statement?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour. Maybe I'm mistaken, but I believe that seven or eight, maybe ten days ago, we received a Chamber ruling regarding a motion for a certain number of witnesses to testify viva voce; and on that list we had the witness who is present here today. And the Court allowed us -- allowed our motion for him to testify viva voce. However, in the way Mr. Stamp has started it appears as if he's going to introduce the statement under 92 ter. I just wanted to intervene in time for you to correct me if I'm mistaken, or are we talking about a 92 ter witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I believe that the decision was that this witness's evidence could be taken pursuant to 92 ter. I wish to just confirm that by getting the decision right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think the determination of this is in the disposition of the judgement, that is, paragraph 19 -- sorry, of the decision; and this decision is a decision of the 10th of February, 2009. And earlier in the decision reference is made to the -- all witnesses for whom we made the application and I think the decision was that the -- the -- only the witnesses Cvetic, Vasiljevic, K84, and K86 shall be heard in the ordinary way, by examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Does that now accord with your recollection, Mr. Djurdjic, now you've had a chance to check?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My assistant has just found the decision, and I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think that means yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, it is my mistake, but the reason is that we received the statements only yesterday, that is, notification of those statements. So I thought that they would only be used as evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on, please, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, I think the last thing you were telling us, Mr. Golubovic, was that you signed your statement of 2002 and that you reviewed it while you were here. In -- at page 3 of the English version of your statement you have said -- maybe this is -- could we perhaps bring it up, this is the document 65 ter number 05133. If we could turn to page 3 of the English, and I think it's the corresponding -- the same page in the B/C/S copy. You will see the first sentence of that page in Serbian refers to ethnic Albanians. Is that expression correct, or is there a change you want to make to that expression?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: I think that we shouldn't have put ethnic Albanians but simply Albanians. So I think what should be stated is that at issue we're Albanians, because I never used the term "ethnic Albanians" but only "Albanians."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, apart from that change is the contents of this statement true to the best of your knowledge and belief; that is, would you make the same answers if you were asked again about the contents?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: I assume that the contents are correct and I would probably provide the same answers, maybe using different words; but in substance, the answers would be the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You tender the statement, do you, Mr. Stamp?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00352, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you, Mr. Golubovic, attend here in The Hague in -- on the 27th of November, 2006, and testified in the trial of Milutinovic and others?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And have you had an opportunity, since you have returned here over the last few days, to review the tape-recording -- audio-recording of the evidence you gave, the questions you were asked and your answers?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, I did have that opportunity in the course of last week, I heard the tapes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And the answers you gave, are they true to the best of your knowledge and belief, in the sense that they would remain the same if you were asked those questions again?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: I think they would be the same. I just said that I may have used a couple of other words or expressed myself differently because I don't know the exact wording I used, so maybe there would be some changes in the order of the words or things like that. But regarding the facts, the facts would remain the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I tender that evidence, Your Honours, that it also be received in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The 65 ter number is 05132.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00353, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Two did you say or 3?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P00353, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to bring up on the screen a map of Serbia so that we could just orientate ourselves to the places the witness is speaking about. 0001, that's a 65 ter number and I think I'm making an indication that it is now P2. And I'd like to zoom to the right of the map just to cover -- if you could zoom out a little bit more.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. This is -- let us just have a look at this first, Witness. This is a part of eastern Serbia. Can you identify where Bor is; that is, where your SUP was located? Maybe you could circle with a pen, please. Thank you very much. If ...

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And can you circle the area of Kladovo, which is the police station that you speak of in your statement?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Only the municipality of Kladovo or -- that is, the town or the entire municipality?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The town.

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And can you make out the area of Tekija where the truck was found in the Danube?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And the -- thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So I think it's self-evident, Your Honours, because the names of the places are there where he circled. I think the circling is adequate identification of the places.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you -- could you tell me, the blue line you see there is the river Danube at the border of Serbia and Romania?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, it is. The Danube is marked in blue, and the border is additionally marked in red.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honours, could this be given an exhibit number as well?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00354, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In your evidence in the Milutinovic trial, you told us that you received information that there was a refrigerator truck in the Danube and it contained some 20 to 30 bodies; that you went to the Kladovo police station, where you were briefed by the police, and they told you that the inscription on the truck indicated that the truck was from Prizren, in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just for the record, Your Honour, that is at page 7411 of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You also said that you were told by the police who briefed you that they were dressed in civilian clothing, also at page 7411 of the transcript; and you were also told by the person who briefed you that there were men and women, again 7411 of the transcript. And in your statement and also in the transcript, in your statement particularly at page 3, you said when you phoned your superior officer, General Djordjevic, to report to him, you briefed him and told him everything that you had been told by those persons who had briefed you at the Kladovo police station; is that correct? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: I do, I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And you briefed him on all those things that I just mentioned that you said you were told?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: I stated as much at the trial, giving evidence, that the information I received from the chief of the department at Kladovo and others who were present at the meeting, that I passed on that information to General Djordjevic; that is, the information that I had received I passed on to the general over the phone.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. And you said, later on in the night it was discovered that there were more than 20 to 30 bodies in the truck, actually there were approximately 50 more corpses in the truck. When you spoke to General Djordjevic later on, did you brief him as well on that?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, most probably during the third or fourth conversation that night I passed that on to him, but then I didn't call him from Kladovo but from Tekija.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I see. You said at page 4 of your statement and also in your evidence, and that's transcript page 7417, that General Djordjevic instructed you to have the lorry destroyed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours, but I don't know whether this is the correct technique that is used by my learned friend, Mr. Stamp. If he wants to give a summary of the statement, that's fine, but let him introduce it as such. But this way, interpreting it and drawing very important conclusions in a general manner and asking the witness whether that is the case without the witness being able to give -- to say his -- to speak his mind about these things, I think this isn't right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The concern of the Chamber is a slightly different one, Mr. Stamp, but perhaps to similar effect. We have both the statement and we have the transcript, and you're now effectively going over parts of it and not eliciting anything new or additional. You're simply getting parts of it you want --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- being mentioned again.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I don't think that is entirely necessary. I was leading up to a question I wanted to ask him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well perhaps if you could move to the question fairly quickly with as brief an introduction as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I just realised through my friends that I had forgotten to read the summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'd been waiting for the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I wonder if now is an appropriate time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. For the record, I just now read a summary of the evidence contained in this statement and the transcript of the witness's evidence. In 1999 Mr. Golubovic was a chief of the secretariat for internal affairs in Bor, Serbia. He held that position from 1992 until his retirement in 2001. Mr. Golubovic will testify with respect to the nature of the organisation -- sorry, to the nature and meaning of a number of Ministry of Internal Affairs documents. Mr. Golubovic testifies that on the evening of the 6th of April, 1999, he received a telephone call from Mr. Tomo Miladinovic, the chief of the criminal investigation section in the SUP -- in the SUP for Bor, that a refrigerator truck containing corpses had been removed from the Danube River near the police station in Kladovo in an area known as Tekija. He went to the police station in Kladovo and contacted the Ministry of Interior -- or internal affairs in Belgrade where he spoke with the accused Djordjevic, the head of the public security service. General Djordjevic telephoned him back shortly thereafter and instructed him that the bodies were to be removed from the refrigerator truck and buried in Kladovo that night. The head of internal affairs department for Kladovo, that is, the department of internal affairs for Kladovo, Vukasin Sperlic and other Kladovo police personnel were to organise the removal and burial of the bodies by acquiring a truck, workers, and the necessary tools that were needed. Mr. Golubovic conveyed these instructions and action was taken that night to bring the refrigerator truck up from the edge of the river and to remove the bodies. Mr. Golubovic phoned General Djordjevic later that night and on at least two occasions and informed him that the job couldn't be completed by morning. It was agreed that the bodies were to be transported to Belgrade and later to a destination unknown to the witness. The driver of the witness Ljubinko Ursuljanovic drove the lorry with the bodies to Belgrade where he was met by arrangement by police who then took the lorry from him. Mr. Golubovic testifies that during one of his telephone conversations with General Djordjevic, the accused told him to have the refrigerator lorry destroyed. The accused also told the witness that the case was not to be made public or reported by the media. Mr. Golubovic testifies also that he subsequently asked General Djordjevic to provide him with money so that he could pay the workers for the work they had done, he received that money, 10.000 dinars, and arranged for it to be distributed to the workers. That, Your Honours, is a brief summary of the evidence contained in the statement. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You mentioned you were heading toward a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you wanting to pursue that?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said that the chief of the -- the chief of the criminal police department for the SUP in Bor had received a dispatch, reporting the truck in the Danube from the Kladovo police station. Do you know what happened to that dispatch?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: The dispatch was read out to me, I saw it later on, but I don't know what happened to it later. And I acted in accordance with that dispatch, and I called a briefing meeting at Kladovo. The dispatch had arrived earlier, but this isn't part of my work, and I did not focus on that. There was a defined policy who does what and communications lines were sometimes down because there was bombing, et cetera, so it was only then that that dispatch arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you know if the dispatch remained within the records or the filing system of the Bor SUP criminal department?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: I do not remember -- I don't know, it may have, but it may not have. It's been almost ten years since, and to me it didn't matter much. And I haven't been in contact with these things for ten years. I don't work there anymore. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. You also indicated in your statement and evidence that you contacted General Djordjevic and asked him for money to pay the workers. Can you remember how long after the bodies had been sent off to Belgrade that you contacted General Djordjevic in respect to the money?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: I didn't keep records on when I spoke to who at the time, but it must have been during that night, or rather, in the early morning hours of the 7th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And do you recall approximately how long after that, just approximately if you don't remember precisely, you received the money?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: I was at Bor when -- again, I assume, because I didn't know that this would be happening so I didn't keep records, but four or five days later or maybe a week later.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you remember who brought the money?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Aleksic brought the money, I believe. He was called Cane, who -- he brought it from the ministry in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you know which section of the ministry Aleksic worked at or was attached to?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: I believe that at the time Aleksic worked at the criminal police administration. I'm not -- I can't give you more precise information, but he was part of that administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And who at that time was in charge of the criminal police administration?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: I think the head of the administration at the time was General Ilic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'd like, with your leave, Your Honours, to move on and to show the witness a document, 04129, and that is a 65 ter number. And perhaps it would be easier for the witness if I handed him or give him a copy in his language if I can find one. Here you go. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If you look at the front of the document you see that it is directed to all chiefs of the secretariat of interior, that is -- you are one of the addressees. You see that?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And if you turn and look at the end of the document, that's on the second page, you will see that it is signed on behalf of General Djordjevic; correct?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes. It says PO, that means "pre procurationem," of the assistant minister or for the assistant minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And if we could go back to the front of the document, the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We see at the top the dispatch number 1268 and the date, the 28th of June, 1998.

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, having looked at this document, can you just tell us briefly what was the purpose of this order?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Well, I don't know if I can explain it well, but the purpose was for all secretariats as well as the military itself had their own defence plans in -- in peacetime too. But as in Kosovo at the time, there were some security problems already. The ministry had to send a certain number of personnel down to Kosovo and so did we. We can see here in this dispatch that the ministry demands from all secretariats to deploy a number of their personnel from special police units to go to Kosovo as a part of detachments that were sent there. That is roughly the content of this dispatch, and there are instructions on how it should be done and at what time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And the second-to-last addressee on the front page you see there is the MUP or the chief of the MUP headquarters in Pristina; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes. It says: "The MUP headquarters in Pristina, Chief of Staff. "

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honours, could this document be received?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I believe it's already Exhibit P133.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And the transcript records line 11, page 17, that it's dated the 28th of June; I think it's the 28th of July, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour. I'd now like to show the witness another document, this is 04094, 65 ter number 04094.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you see that or would you like a hard copy?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can I, with the assistance of the usher --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it may be better if I could look at it on paper so you don't have to zoom-in on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: On the face of it this is a dispatch of the 30th of July, 1999 -- sorry, the 30th of July, 1998, and it is stated that it is Re: The RJB's dispatch number 1268 of the 28th of July, 1999 [sic], and at the bottom it indicates that it is from the chief of the secretariat, Colonel Caslav Golubovic. Can you briefly tell the Court what this document is about and how it relates to the previous document I showed to you?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: This is a document which two days after the reception of the other document from the ministry was sent to the ministry. It says that the Bor secretariat's obligation to send a certain number of police officers has been executed and it says how many were summoned, how many were -- were present, how many did not come, et cetera. So it's basically a report about what has been done in accordance with the dispatch that had come in earlier. And it says down there in the signature line that the secretariat is represented by the head, that being me, but there's no signature. So somebody most probably sent it from the police department at Bor to the police department in Belgrade, and that was the current practice at the time and it must -- the original must bear the signature of the one who actually sent it because the previous dispatch had been received from the police administration in Belgrade, the department of public security but the police administration. That is the brief content of this dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you just tell us approximately how often your SUP was required to supply personnel to augment the PJP detachments in Kosovo and Metohija in 1998 and how often in 1999?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic, no previous mention of PJP detachments.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It's in the document, Your Honour, that the witness says --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Not that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I wanted to point out something else. This question is not permissible because my learned friend is saying that the number of members is increasing and this cannot be seen from this dispatch nor can it be found in any statements given by this witness at trial or in his written statements. So he -- the question is: How many times did the number of personnel increase down there. I heard this -- that is the interpretation I received. I'm not looking at the document. The witness can explain what these dispatches mean, but that has not been stated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic is correct, Mr. Stamp. You've moved from one event to asking a question about a number of events without the witness making that connection first.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Was this the only time you were required to dispatch personnel to Kosovo, and that is in 1998 and 1999 we are speaking about?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: I have to say that we didn't send personnel. Only in 1998 and in 1999 the secretariat had -- each secretariat had its own unit, and then every 15 days there was shifts and they went for the needs in Kosovo. Now, whether the numbers were 30, 40, or 80, it depended on the requirements. After 15 or 20 days, the personnel would return to the secretariat, I'm talking about Bor, and then probably they would be replaced by another unit and another number of people from a different secretariat. This was all part of the plan of national defence and the duties of the secretariat, with a view to ensuring a positive security situation in Kosovo. So this was done even before 1998 and after it. Now, how many people went there, this depended on the possibilities. The smaller secretariats with smaller staff sent smaller numbers; and those who were larger and had more personnel would send more. The secretariat in Bor had this special unit which, even in peacetime, was designed for the purpose of security assignments. So we see from this dispatch that 69 members from the reserve force, together with active officers were sent there. As far as I remember, I think that our unit numbered about 90 -- close to that number. I can't remember exactly because this was a long time ago. So a smaller number were went there in relation to the strength of the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: At the beginning of your answer you said this was in 1998 and 1999. Can you remember having regard to your answer about how many times you were required to send personnel to Kosovo in 1999?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: I'm unable to answer that question. I don't know how many times in 1998 and before. As I said before, it wasn't only in 1998 and 1999 but earlier on as well. Now, how many times, I don't know. I just know that the people who were sent there had shifts of 15 days. Now, they may be coming from the secretariat in Bor or the secretariat in Zajecar. They would spend 15 or 20 days there. Then they would come back, and their place would be taken by others. So I don't know how many times this took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could that one be received, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00355, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And with your leave and with the assistance of the usher, could I show to the witness and could I ask that we bring up on the screen document with the 65 ter number 4086, 04086.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I read the summary carefully regarding the points that this witness would be testifying about, I do not see the connection with the document, or rather, what circumstances he has testified about which would prompt this document being shown to him. My understanding was that he was to testify about the discovery of the refrigerator truck, the procedure that followed, and the conversations he had with the general. Now we have here some exhibits that are not linked to that statement, and this is a 92 ter witness. If he was a live witness, then it would be normal for him to testify about other issues as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the notification indicated that the witness was live/92 ter. And I do believe in the summary I read, I indicated that he would testify in respect to the nature and meaning of a number of documents emanating from the Ministry of the Interior. And I can say that having regard to the time this is the last document that I would show to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm sure both counsel are aware that notice is required to be given of material evidence to be given; that doesn't mean that notice is to be given of every single item, if some matter is minor or incidental. I just make that observation to lessen the number of times when it may be of concern to one counsel or another that specific notice of a document has not been given. But in this case, I think what is being done here, Mr. Djurdjic, is in accordance with the general indication given in the notice you had. So carry on, please, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Golubovic, you have had an opportunity to look at that document briefly. On the face of it, it is dispatch number 312, dated the 18th of February, 1999; and you see there that you are one of the addressees. The second addressee is to all the chiefs of the SUPs. You see that?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And if you look at the last page of this document --

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: -- you can see who sent it, who issued it. Can you tell us who issued it?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: It says here assistant minister or chief of public security department, Lieutenant-General Vlastimir Djordjevic. Most probably he is the signatory because we don't see the letters PO. I don't know his handwriting, but his signature should be there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, can you read the signature? Is that ...

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: I read what it says assistant minister, chief of public security department, Lieutenant-General Vlastimir Djordjevic; and below that we see handwriting, the first letter Dj, so most probably it is. I assume that it was signed by General Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you recall receiving and seeing this document while you were still employed to the SUP Bor; that is, on or about the 18th of February, 1999?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Ten years later for me to say that I remember exactly when I received it and saw it, but I'm quite sure that it couldn't have bypassed me because it was addressed to me as one of the 33 chiefs of the secretariats in Serbia. Therefore, I certainly saw it and read it and I certainly did take steps relating to what is stated in this document because that was my duty and obligation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Was it mandatory that the addressees abide -- or obeyed the instructions given in this document?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Certainly it was mandatory for all of us as part of the organisation and the plans for All People's Defence, and as this was the period prior to the bombing campaign and the aggression that was just a month prior to that event, so we had to obey and we certainly did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I see. But if you look at the addressees you will see the last addressee is the RDB, the state security department, and you will see it says: "To the chief for information ..." Would the -- would the chief of the RDB subordinated to General Djordjevic or can you elaborate on that for us?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: You're asking me --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said -- yes, please. Just to clarify something. You said that all of the addressees were obliged to obey the instructions contained in this document, but I see here that the last addressee, it is sent to him for information and I note also that he was the chief of the RDB. Can you explain that -- just clarify that for us?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: I can explain. I realise now what you are asking me. Mr. Prosecutor. It says here that a copy of this document was sent to the head of the State Security Service for his information but not to take the measures envisioned by this dispatch, for him to be informed, and for him to know what is being done. So this is a normal relationship between services to -- for them to coordinate. So I think the head of the state security department was not subordinate to the head of the public security department.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. So, therefore, I take it that your evidence is, apart from him the others were obliged to obey the instructions contained therein?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, each one within his own competencies, because here we also have the staff of the ministry in Pristina, the commanders of these detachments, each one of them had the obligation, not only pursuant to this -- these instructions, but pursuant to the plans that were adopted earlier on, they had to act in accordance with those plans and to take security measures when the need arises.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't intend to take you through all of it, but if we could look at page 3 in the English version, and I think it is page 3 on your document as well in Serbian; but it is item numbered 7 in the document, paragraph numbered 7 in the document. It says: "Through intensified intelligence and other measures at actions, carry out the necessary checks, compile lists, and establish complete control over voluntary" -- sorry, "over volunteer and paramilitary units and their members." In your SUP were there volunteer and paramilitary units?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: I think there were no voluntary or paramilitary units within the. territory of the secretariat. There may have been individual volunteers who reported to someone else somewhere else to those units if any such existed at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you know where the volunteer and paramilitary units were?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: No, I don't know, except what appeared later on in the media, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. If we could move on to the last page of this document, both int the English and the B/C/S version, it's a paragraph numbered 7 -- sorry, numbered 17. It goes on 17: "If members of the PJP are engaged outside the Secretariat's territory, other Ministry employees and members of the police reserve force who have not been employed in a PJP shall engaged in the Secretariat's area to carry out tasks and assignments that come within the Ministry's competence." At that time leading up to and during the NATO intervention, did you have or were there any members of the PJP in your SUP assigned to Kosovo? And I'm just speaking of that period from the 18th of May to the end of the NATO intervention -- I'm sorry, from the 18th of February, 1999, the date of this document, to the end of the NATO intervention?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. Prosecutor, could you repeat the question once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I apologise. Were members of your SUP assigned to Kosovo in that period, that is, policemen from your SUP?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: You mean in the period just before the beginning of the aggression?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And during the aggression.

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, they were. I told you a moment ago that every 15 days when our turn came a part of the members of the special police units would go there for these security assignments in Kosovo in the period prior to the aggression and in the period during the aggression; but they were not stationed there permanently but only for a certain period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Golubovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could that document be received in evidence, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00356, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And that, may it please you, is the additional questions I wanted to ask in addition the statement and the transcript. May it please Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Stamp, and it's encouraging to see that you finished within time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I was trying very hard to ensure that we don't go over the time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We commend your efforts and are sure that you will continue to show that spirit. Looking at the time, it might be better for Mr. Djurdjic if we had the adjournment now and you could then commence after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, that would suit the Defence very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We'll have the first break now and resume at ten minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Golubovic, my name is Veljko Djurdjic. I'm a member of the Defence team for the accused, Vlastimir Djordjevic. My assistants are here, Ms. Marie and Ms. Jelena Dzambazovic as members of the team, and the lead counsel is working on the preparations for the Defence case. Mr. Golubovic, I would like to start from your statements at today's proceedings and then we will look at the other evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like Exhibit 133 to be called up on the e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Golubovic, would you agree with me if I say that this is a typical logistic behaviour of the police administration regarding the engagement and sending of units of the police by decision of the minister?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: I said a moment ago that this was a customary and regular practice. We would receive instructions, and we would act in accordance with those instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that we are talking about sending units to an assignment outside the territory of their home territory, of their home SUP?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that in this kind of dispatch there is no indication about the activities of the unit that is being sent into the field?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: We never knew exactly where the unit would be except what it says in the dispatch, that we ensure a certain number of personnel, the logistics, the transportation, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Talking about logistics, let us try and explain to the Chamber the police administration, or rather, the police department in the SUP carried out all the logistic preparations to ensure a PJP unit from within the SUP, the SUPs in the territory of the republic, for them to be ready once the minister takes a decision to activate them; am I right?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right when I say that upon sending a PJP unit outside your own territory have no further information regarding the activities of the unit and their assignments?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: You are quite right. That is how it was. I rarely knew where the unit was, except if certain individuals from the unit would call up and contact their homes. As for their deployment in Kosovo, we were not familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that you received information only in the event of disease, injury, or death of a member of the PJP sent from your secretariat?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, that is how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I also right if I say that the material and financial aspects of the engagement of that unit outside the secretariat were realised within the secretariat from which they were sent?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, their per diems were paid out there, everything else that they needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Would you agree then that all the activities that we have listed and that were carried out within the framework of the SUP and the police department, all this was logistic support for the units who performed assignments determined by the minister and upon instructions from the minister?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Evidence of this is also the fact that you referred to, on the second page of this telegram, that somebody else signed this telegram by authority of the name indicated?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: That was the case with most of these dispatches and telegrams that we received and those that we sent from the secretariat. I hardly remember actually signing any telegram, though my title and my name was printed on all of those dispatches. This was signed by someone working in the police department and especially within the framework of defensive preparations, that was the organisation and the procedure applied.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I now have Exhibit PBR -- under 65 ter Prosecution P4086, though it was given an exhibit number today, 350 I think. The decision dated the 18th of February, 1999 -- sorry, 356 in the e-court, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Golubovic, could we slowly look through this decision to see what its purpose was, bearing in mind to whom it was addressed and the time -- the timing of it. Mr. Golubovic, am I right in saying that this dispatch was addressed to all SUPs in the territory of Serbia without any discrimination?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was the addressee also the staff of the ministry in Pristina, the head of that staff?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, that is what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Will you please confirm whether your head is indicated as a recipient?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, that is what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: As it says the chief of the SUP, because it must be indicated who the addressee is.

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, you read out under paragraph 3, maybe I'm wrong -- would you read it now. The letters are very small for me where it says: To the commander 1 to 35. On page 1 at the top, the heading, the addressee, above RDB.

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, it says to SPP --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you translate that, what SPP stands for.

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Station of border police. Border police stations, because they also were attached to the secretariat. So a secretariat always had a border station attached to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Golubovic. Am I right in saying that the recipient is not a single unit of the PJP?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: No, the police stations were not indicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What I'm saying is that among the addressees there's not a single PJP unit?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You explained, but this dispatch was sent to the head of a different department of the ministry for his information so that he should be familiarised with the measures being taken within the framework of public security and in connection with the situation.

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I told the Prosecutor a moment ago, that this was simply for his information so that he should know what was being done in the public security secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you agree with me that members of the public security could not issue orders to members of the state security and vice versa, members of the state security could not issue instructions to you?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that it was only the minister who could combine the activities of the two departments and form special bodies, including members of both departments, and that only he could issue instructions to such bodies that he had formed?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: I think only the minister because both the state security department and the public security departments were, in terms of their functions and organisations, quite separate. They were not one institution, but they were within the framework of the ministry and under the authority of the minister, of course, who combined the activities of both those organisational units.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And this rule could only be changed by the minister by his decision, who would also stipulate how this would function in future?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Golubovic, I'm not sure whether you can see this properly or shall I give you a hard copy? Am I right - I'm putting it in this way to speed things up - that this dispatch was addressed to the addressees in view of the preparations for the -- for a possible aggression, firstly; and secondly, to prevent the spreading of terrorist activities to other parts of the republic; and also to mitigate the possible consequences of the aggression; and to normalise living conditions. So in addition to regular activities certain measures needed to be taken, which were listed here; am I right?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, you are, because that is what is stated in this dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there mention anywhere of any anti-terrorist activities in Kosovo or the activities of any units in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us move on. Mr. Golubovic, in any normal country, does the Ministry of the Interior have plans for the eventuality of war?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Most probably. I am not aware of what happens in other countries, but in our country even in peacetime this was normal, as I worked there for many years, regardless of the regimes in power, the communist, or any other there were these defence plans.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And would you agree that those defence plans would start from the ministry through the SUPs to the lowest-level organisational units within the MUP?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it normal that at a time when aggression against the state is expected that preparational measures are taken to defend against the aggression?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: That should be normal.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me pass on to item 2, that is, that part about the preparation of units for possible war is very short. Do you agree that under item 2 what is said is a stronger engagement of all units of the ministry, an intensification of activities, monitoring the movements of NATO forces, especially from the territories of the former republics of Macedonia and Bosnia-Herzegovina, as well as other activities that threaten security.

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: I agree, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does item 3 mention the planning and training of -- of supervisors for the implementation of wartime rules?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does item 4 include the training of untrained members of both active units and reserve units?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: I don't have these items on the screen; I can't read them. Which items did you mention?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Item 4.

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: That's what we did before that too. We trained the reservists possibly once a year, and the other activities were conducted with active staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does item 5 mention the selection of alternative locations?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, that's what we did in practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Item 6 mentions the planning for the increase of beat duty patrols, and other activities, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we've arrived at item 7 about which the Prosecutor asked you. Am I right in saying that item 7 doesn't contain any provisions about the use of volunteer and paramilitary units?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: There's no mention of that. It only says that through cooperative work and other measures and actions it should be checked whether there are such units in the areas covered by the secretariat. I have already said to the Prosecutor that in our area there were -- there wasn't a single paramilitary or volunteer unit established; but there must have been individuals who had reported outside the area of our secretariat to participate in volunteer units, become members of those units, but that there were no such individuals in our area.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it right that this stipulates preventive actions?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, and we should report to our superior bodies if we observe that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Golubovic, am I right in saying that during the war at Kosovo and Metohija there were no paramilitary units?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: From my secretariat and as far as I know, there were none, none from the secretariat of Bor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that volunteers could be engaged during the war in Kosovo and Metohija only through the procedures carried out by the military bodies?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: I remember that there were instructions for all the volunteers to report to the secretariat of people's defence, but they didn't report to us, not to the police. And as far as I know from the press and other media, they were put under the control of the Army of Serbia or of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Does item 9 foresee the planning and increased control and regulation of traffic?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: That is normal, that's part of our daily routine, it's only intensified in extraordinary conditions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Does item 10 foresee the carrying out of preparations and checks that all types of communication, cryptographic, data protection are functioning?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does item 13 say that checks must be carried out and that must remain sure that there is sufficient equipment of the firefighters?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, they were also part of the secretariat of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does it foresee in -- increased measures for the protection against fire?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So we needn't go on like this. So this is normal preparation for wartime situation in case it should arise. And now let's move on to item 17. Am I right in saying that this item instructs you for the eventuality of the engagement of your PJP unit outside the area of your secretariat the reserve forces of the police shall be deployed in a PJP?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: That's what we did routinely when they were not there because we would be left with a small number of staff in the secretariat, and that's when we called in some of our reservists and these others who performed similar tasks at the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So let us move from the abstract level down to concrete things. Does that mean that a criminal police inspector, usually dealing with homicide, say, would carry out the duties of a car patrol?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, they would fill in the gaps as necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that item 18 instructs you to cooperate with other state bodies and institutions to normalise life and the mitigation of possible -- the possible consequences of aggression?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can we summarise this as follows, does this -- is it right to say that this telegram doesn't contain anything peculiar to Kosovo and Metohija but that it -- but rather, that it refers to the overall situation in the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: I think that is indeed the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please call up Exhibit P57 from e-court, which -- it's on page -- it's page 2. The -- it's page 1 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Golubovic, you can now see on the screen a decision of the Ministry of the Interior dated the 16th of June, 1998. We'll go back to page 1, but I'm interested in item 2 now. I will read out to you to make it easier for you.

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: I cannot see item 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now you can see it: "It's the duty of the staff to plan, organise, and lead or supervise the work and the engagement of the organisational units of the ministry as well as the deployed and attached units to -- in combatting terrorism in the area of the autonomous province of Kosovo and Metohija." Am I right in saying, sir, that the minister by this decision authorised the staff for the purpose of the combatting of terrorism in the autonomous province of Kosovo and Metohija to plan, organise, and supervise the SUPs as well as other deployed and attached units?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: That's what it reads and that's most probably how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does this second paragraph of item 2 say that: "Apart from these tasks, the staff also had to plan, organise, direct, and coordinate the work of the organisational units of the ministry in Kosovo and Metohija in the carrying out of more complex and special security tasks"?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, well that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: A minute ago we spoke about the relationship between the two departments. So before we return to page 1, here, after the part where certain individuals are mentioned by name, it reads: "For the member of the broader staff," or rather, "the chiefs of the SUPs of the centres and departments of RDB in the area of Kosovo and Metohija are also appointed members of the staff."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the Defence counsel please repeat the last part of his question; we didn't catch that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it true that ... I will repeat the question. I seem to have gone fast. Am I right in saying that this paragraph says that the organisational units of public and state security in Kosovo and Metohija are also parts of the broad -- broader staff?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that only the minister could establish a staff comprising people from both departments and determine how they will organise and to who they will report?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Under the law and other regulations he coordinated the activities of both these departments, both state security and public security.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it true -- is it correct that item 3 says that: "The work of the staff and the security situation from the framework of the duties of the staff, the Chief of Staff will report to the minister"?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just one more thing. Am I right in saying that item 6 states that the minister orders all previous decisions to be overruled by this decision?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please put the following document on the screen, Exhibit P67 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Golubovic, this is a decision of the minister dated the 31st of May, 1999, about the establishment of the military staff for the suppression of terrorism. I would like to focus your attention on page 3 of the decision, the last page, that is, the very end. Does this paragraph say that the minister ordered this decision to overrule the decision dated June the 16th?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't want to continue reading this decision because it is identical to the previous one. Mr. Golubovic, please take a look at Exhibit P75 from e-court. Mr. Golubovic, can you see that this is a decision by the minister -- by Minister Stojiljkovic, dated 4 June 1997, by which Bosko Petric is appointed chief of the secretariat of the interior in Pristina in effect of 15th of June, 1997, and for a term of two years?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, I saw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do tell me, please, the last paragraph, the minister orders that one copy be forwarded to the persons in question; one to the secretariat where he used to work; another to the secretariat where he's being sent; and another to the legal department of this ministry?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that this was forwarded to the legal department of this ministry to regulate the status of the person in question because he is sent from one organisational unit to the other?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please call up Exhibit P78 from e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Golubovic, am I right if I say that by this decision of the 15th of April, 1999, the minister, Vlajko Stojiljkovic, in the case of Vucina Janijicevic is appointing him to head of the secretariat in Kosovska Mitrovica -- Vucina Janijicevic is being appointed to the Kosovska Mitrovica secretariat of the interior.

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, that is what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you, Mr. Golubovic, the minister has the right, according to law, to apply prescribed methods of leadership which he himself has prescribed, and to amend them and to decide about certain competencies of other persons. In this particular case because of the significance of the security situation in Kosovo, the minister himself decided on the appointment of the chief of the department of the interior?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, that was what happened in practice. He could dismiss a chief, he could transform him to another secretariat, he could give him different assignments within the territory of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Under the list of 65 ter Prosecution Exhibit P01879, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Golubovic, is it right that by this decision the minister, Vlajko Stojiljkovic, is appointing Colonel Dusan Gavranic to the position of chief of the SUP in Gnjilane, effective as of the 1st of January, 1999?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you know that Mr. Gavranic, before being sent there, was the chief of the SUP in Zrenjanin --

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So a chief of SUP from a part of the territory outside of Kosovo is being sent by the minister to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could this document be admitted into evidence, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be D00038, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I would now like to move on to laws, as you have a degree in law and you have passed the examination for judges.

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, but I haven't been involved in those activities for a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, but we'll be dealing about police regulations now, which you are familiar with.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I have Exhibit 166 [as interpreted] to be called up in the e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let me tell you in the meantime, Mr. Golubovic, this is the Law on Internal Affairs --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm being told that the transcript is incorrect. It says 166, and it should be P66.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let me draw your attention to Article 7 of this law, page 2 of the English version. Am I right, Mr. Golubovic, that the minister determines the manner in which the Ministry of the Interior performs its duties and issues instructions for their performance?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, all the instructions and guide-lines were prescribed by the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it right to say that the minister reports on his work only at the request to the National Assembly and to the president of the Republic of Serbia with regard to security activities?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: That was how it was according to the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now move on to Article 27. It is page 9 of the English version. Page -- in the Serbian text it is page 3 and page 9 of the English version, Article 27. These are provisions regarding reserve forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it right to say that in case of an imminent threat of war or war the Ministry of the Interior should be brought up to strength with conscripts from the reserve force of the ministry?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that when the conditions were fulfilled, the minister could decide that even in peacetime the reserve force should be engaged to perform certain duties within the terms of reference of the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, we had such cases in practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that this is regulated by Article 28 of this law and that those persons who are engaged from the reserve forces when performing these duties have the status of authorised officials?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, they wore a uniform, and they were given instructions from their superiors in the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that they were entitled to remuneration and other social insurance entitlements while they were engaged for these purposes?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Was it customary to train the reserve force within the plan?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, they were engaged for training also and for performing certain tasks, so they were engaged on those two grounds.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us now examine page 21 and 22 of the English version and page 6 of the Serbian version, Article 72.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Golubovic, am I right in saying that by virtue of this article it is possible to assign MUP members from one organisational unit to go to other organisational units within the territory of the Republic of Serbia and that on the basis of this law they may perform these duties from 30 days up to one year?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, we had such cases in practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that this was the basis for the minister to send certain individuals to work in Kosovo and Metohija or upon his authorisation another person on his behalf?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, in the secretariat in Bor we had several cases when persons were assigned to assist in Prizren, and I can't remember what other town, but they would go there for 15 days or 30 days on the basis of a decision from the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now -- could the usher assist us and put on the ELMO P69.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Golubovic, this is the law on the state administration which was also applied to organs of the Ministry of the Interior; you will agree with me?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see page 4 in the Serbian version and page 2 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And Article 43 of this law which prescribes that: The minister in accordance with the law is in charge of the ministry?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And Article 44 says that the minister shall organise a lawful performance of duties and decide about the rights and duties of the employees -- rights, duties, and responsibilities of the employees?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In paragraph 2 of this article it is stated that the minister shall be responsible for carrying out the function for which he has been entrusted and for the work of the ministry, so he is the responsible official, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Article 46, Mr. Golubovic, says that assistant ministers shall be appointed in the ministry to head certain departments and carry out tasks specified in the document on job organisation and planning and other duties which the minister may entrust to them. And paragraph 2 says that the assistant ministers shall be appointed by the government. Would you agree with me that the assistant ministers were appointed persons by the government?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that those appointed persons were -- defined the areas in which they would assist the minister by the minister?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that there are no limitations regarding the determination of activities that individual assistants will assist him with?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: I assume that you are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that there are no higher- or lower-level assistant ministers but that they are persons of equal status?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: I think so. Now, it's another matter whether someone has a more- or less-important job, but they were all treated on equal footing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: The job of the assistant minister is to assist the minister with regard to certain issues determined by the minister; am I right?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And for the activities for which he has been appointed as an assistant.

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes, but we've seen that the minister determines those areas and that he's appointed by the government.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right that one assistant minister cannot issue orders to another assistant minister, in view of the fact that they can receive instructions for their work only from the minister?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: That is how it should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now call up exhibit -- Defence Exhibit D0020357, if it could be called up, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Golubovic, it is the rules on the internal organisation of the Ministry of the Interior and the revised version, and it came into force on the 31st of December, 1997. Mr. Golubovic, let us first explain. These rules actually pertain only to the department of public security because Article 2 says that special rules will be adopted for other departments; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: I can see only the front page. I can't see anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I will read out page 1 to you: "Republic of Serbia, Ministry of the Interior, official secret, highly confidential -- strictly confidential. "Rules on the internal organisation of the Ministry of the Interior, revised version," and it says, "Belgrade, the 31st of December, 1997. "The activities from the purview of the Ministry of the Interior, that is, public security, personal safety of the citizens, the prevention of crimes and the catching of the perpetrators of crimes, providing security at public gatherings, the safety of traffic, the control of the passing of the state border, the control of movement in the -- along the borders, control of the movement of foreigners, control of the possession of fire-arms, as well as the control over the -- over explosive devices, fire-fighting, citizenship, numbers of citizens, and other activities as is set out by the law, and the basic organisational unit is the department of public security." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, Article 3 describes local jurisdiction of the secretariats of the interior. Let me explain because I didn't finish earlier, that the Bor secretariat was in charge of the municipalities of Kladovo, Majdanpek, and Negotin?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Speaking about your secretariat, would it be right to say that in your territory you had departments of the interior at Kladovo, Negotin, and Majdanpek; and the secretariat carried out these tasks directly for Bor?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC.
utterances.text: For Bor, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
